Comparison of CO desorption from ECCOsorb-1 using external heating and Joule heating 2 Sorbent Manufacturing Scale-Up After validation of the electrically conductive nonwoven substrate and the performance of the sorbent coated filter samples, the commercial partner commenced preparation of the pilot-scale filter manufacturing line to coat ECCOsorb-T1 onto the selected filter substrates. As part of the preparation process, the commercial partner required a minimum of 50 kg of ECCOsorb-T1 to operate the pilot manufacturing line. Susteon scaled its sorbent synthesis procedure from 25 g batches of sorbent to 2.5 kg batches, producing 20 batches to meet the minimum amount needed. The section discusses the modifications to the synthesis procedure made to scale the process safely and cost effectively and the QA/QC performed to verify batch to batch consistency. Initially, the lab-scale synthetic procedure was modified to minimize the use of costly and hazardous organic solvents. An organic solvent was used in each reaction step, including washing and functionalization, of the original sorbent synthesis, which can be cost prohibitive for commercial-scale manufacturing. Alternative ECCOsorb-T1 synthetic procedures were developed that substituted some or all the organic solvent with water. The impact of solvent was evaluated by analyzing the equilibrium capacities of ECCOsorb-T1 synthesized and washed with organic solvent, ECCOsorb-T1 synthesized in organic solvent and washed with water, and ECCOsorb-1 synthesized and washed with water. For further scale-up, water was used as the solvent for all reaction steps. Additional equipment for large scale sorbent synthesis was procured, including mechanical mixers, pumps, containers, and drying equipment.
